Synchronous Fireflies
You logged 10 flash patterns — enough to earn the swarm's trust. Photinus carolinus, the Smokies' famous synchronous firefly, is one of the only species in North America that flashes in unison: for about two weeks every June near Elkmont, thousands of males pulse together in the dark.

The swarm now spirals around you in a synchronized display — and your stamina is fully restored. Catch and release 10 more on any clear night to see it again. You earned the swarm's trust. Photinus carolinus flashes in unison — they now spiral around you and your stamina is restored.
